item.title: Kamaage Udon: Fresh-Boiled Sanuki Noodles — Guide
item.description: Kamaage udon is one of the simplest and most beloved ways to eat Sanuki udon, prized for tasting the noodles at their freshest. Rather than being rinsed in cold water (which firms them up), the udon are served straight from the boiling pot — ‘kama-age’, lifted from the cauldron — still sitting in their hot, starchy cooking water in a wooden tub or bowl. You dip them into a small cup of warm, concentrated dashi broth, often with ginger and spring onion, and eat them soft, slippery and warm, full of the pure flavour and aroma of freshly boiled wheat.
